title: Demultiplex batch signals and simplify KV epoch coordinator to reduce tail latency
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Our continuous-batcher uses a global signal/condition variable to wake worker lanes when a batch is ready. Under high concurrency this causes head-of-line lock contention and jitter in wake latencies, which amplifies tail latency for small interactive requests. The KV epoch coordinator maintains a single global epoch state and serial GC/compaction passes which further block short-lived requests during maintenance windows.

Goal: Reduce p95/p99 tail latency for interactive inference by: 1) demultiplexing batch-ready signals into per-shard/per-core queues with lock-free wake paths; 2) replacing the single global KV epoch state with a lightweight per-shard epoch vector and cooperative compaction that avoids long pauses; 3) standardize APIs so the scheduler can opportunistically bypass heavy paths for latency-sensitive lanes.

Scope: Refactor continuous batch signaling, introduce per-shard eventfd-based wake queues, redesign KV epoch coordinator to per-shard epochs with async compaction, update metrics and tracing for the new flow, and a small dependency bump for our concurrency primitives library. Includes unit, integration, and load testing and a canary rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: p95 tail latency for short (<100 token) interactive requests improves by >=15% under 90th-percentile load profile compared to baseline
no regression in throughput (within 5%) for batch-heavy workloads in Dedicated tests
KV compaction runs no longer introduce pauses >50ms on average for small requests
new per-shard wake metrics and epoch metrics are emitted to Console dashboards
integration tests covering epoch rollover, shard rebalancing, and fast-path bypass pass in CI
technical_notes: Replace global condition variable used by continuous-batcher with per-shard wake queues. Each shard exposes a lock-free ring buffer + eventfd to signal workers — reduces cross-core cache thrash.

Introduce 'epoch_vector' in KV engine: small fixed-size array of u64 epochs, one per shard. Coordinator advances shard epochs independently and triggers compaction for shards whose epoch delta exceeds threshold.

Compaction becomes cooperative: background compactor threads request short quiesce windows from a shard and compact in small segments to avoid long GC pauses. Short requests take fast-path token-hits if compaction pending.
Scheduler changes: add a latency-sensitive lane tag; routing can steer requests to worker lanes that avoid shards currently undergoing segment compaction.
Minimal dependency upgrade: bump 'concurrency-helpers' internal lib from 2.3.1 -> 2.4.0 for the new MPMC ring API. Run full compat tests — no ABI break expected but verify under load.

Locking trade-offs: move from coarse global mutex to per-shard atomics and small per-shard spinlocks where strictly necessary. Accept slightly higher memory overhead for per-shard state to reduce contention.

Backwards compatibility: public API surface remains unchanged. Internal scheduling config flags gate the new behavior and default to 'on' for canary nodes. Provide runtime flag to disable per-shard mode if needed.
implementation_plan: Spike (2d): prototype per-shard ring + eventfd wake path in a small micro-benchmark. Measure wake latency and CPU overhead.
Core refactor (5d): swap batcher signaling to per-shard queues, update unit tests, add new metrics (wake_latency_ms, wakes_per_sec/shard).
KV coordinator (5d): implement epoch_vector, cooperative compactor API, and compaction chunking. Add integration hooks so scheduler can query shard state.
Scheduler integration (3d): add lane tagging, implement routing policy in ingress dispatcher to prefer non-compacting shards for latency lanes.
Testing & canary (4d): run dedicated load profiles, run mixed interactive/batching CI scenarios, deploy canary to 10% of serving fleet, monitor dashboards.
test_plan: Unit tests for ring buffer, eventfd wake semantics, and epoch vector transitions.
Integration test: simulate shard rebalancing while compaction running and validate no lost requests and eventual consistency of epochs.
Performance test: run the 90th-percentile interactive profile (500rps small requests + background batches) on scaled perf cluster and compare p50/p95/p99 to baseline.
Chaos test: trigger background compaction task timeouts and validate scheduler fallback routes and no request starvation.
End-to-end canary validation: monitor wake_latency_ms, compactor_chunk_duration, KV_eviction_rate, and user-facing tail-latency metrics in Console.
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag 'per_shard_batch_signals' default=true for new nodes; can be disabled via admin Console.
Deploy to internal staging, run full e2e perf suite, then promote to a small canary subset (10% of serving fleet) for 48 hours.
If canary stable, widen to 50% for 24 hours, then full rollout. Keep rollback steps documented in the runbook.
Post-rollout: keep enhanced metrics for 7 days and run top-down tail-latency analysis; revert if we see >5% regression in any major customer flow.
risks: Regression in batch throughput if per-shard partitioning causes imbalance — mitigated by shard hotness rebalancer and telemetry.
Subtle correctness bugs during epoch transitions leading to stale reads — mitigated by strict integration tests and a short double-write validation mode in canary.
Dependency upgrade causing unexpected scheduling behavior on older kernel builds — will run compatibility matrix across our supported AMIs.
comments: 2025-02-13 Maya Chen: Spike completed. Micro-benchmarks show wake latency median 6us (down from 32us) and 2-3x reduction in tail jitter on a 48-vCPU node. CPU overhead for per-shard ring ~1.8%.
2025-02-18 Arjun Patel: Implemented initial eventfd ring adapter. Opening PR for review. Observed a regression in batch throughput when shard hotness concentrated — adding shard-rebalancer hook.
2025-02-21 Review (SRE): Please add observability for compaction backpressure. Suggested emitting backlog gauge so we can detect build-up before p99 rises. Added to commits.
2025-02-24 Design feedback (PM - Elena Ruiz): Ensure feature flag is off by default for Dedicated reserved instances until we validate cost/perf tradeoffs. Will gate by tenant tier in config.

2025-02-27 QA (Arjun): Integration tests for epoch rollover failing intermittently under simulated network partitions. Root cause suspected race in epoch vector update; implementing CAS loop to harden transition.

2025-03-01 Arjun Patel: Stabilized epoch CAS logic and added a short double-write verification mode for canary (keeps shadow writes to old path and compares results for 5 minutes). All unit tests green; running perf harness now.
